# NetScope

> NetScope is an installable, client-side network security toolkit that runs entirely in the browser as a static site with no backend. It checks your public IP and approximate location, measures connection speed, looks up email breaches and checks passwords against Have I Been Pwned using k-anonymity (only a 5-character SHA-1 prefix leaves the page), generates passwords and passphrases with Web Crypto, and grades a domain's DNS and email security (SPF, DMARC, DKIM, DNSSEC, MTA-STS, TLS reporting, BIMI) over DNS-over-HTTPS. It is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with a strict Content-Security-Policy, MIT licensed.

## Live demo

- [Landing page](https://patrickking67.github.io/netscope/): what NetScope does and how it handles your data
- [Toolkit](https://patrickking67.github.io/netscope/pages/app.html): the five tools and Full Scan; works as a guest
- [About](https://patrickking67.github.io/netscope/pages/about.html): privacy summary and the services each tool calls

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/patrickking67/netscope): full source on GitHub
- [core.js](https://github.com/patrickking67/netscope/blob/main/assets/js/core.js): pure, unit-tested logic for hashing, breach parsing, DNS grading, entropy and speed math
- [app.js](https://github.com/patrickking67/netscope/blob/main/assets/js/app.js): DOM wiring, network calls and rendering
- [Tests](https://github.com/patrickking67/netscope/tree/main/tests): node:test suites for core logic, pages and the service worker
